questions.stem: On White space use: a designer reviewing a research institute's poster presentation notices that a flyer packs text and images with almost no empty areas. What is the most likely effect of this crowding?

options.text: Stronger color harmony between all of the elements
options.misconception: confuses empty space with relationships between colors

options.text: Automatic symmetry of the overall composition
options.misconception: mistakes the density of spacing for mirrored balance

options.text: Reduced legibility and no visual resting places for the eye
Greater closure because all the shapes are touching
options.misconception: misapplies shape completion to a crowded arrangement

questions.explanation: White space, or negative space, gives elements room to breathe and defines the gaps that separate groups. When a flyer is crowded, the eye has no resting point and the hierarchy blurs, so adding empty space improves clarity rather than wasting area.
questions.hint: Consider what the empty areas between elements actually do.

questions.learningObjective: evaluate x-height differences in a design critique
questions.stem: On X-height differences: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that two settings use the same point size but one appears larger. What best explains the difference in apparent size?

options.text: Point size measures visible ink height and always matches the appearance
options.misconception: misstates what a point size value actually measures

options.text: The face with the larger x-height has proportionally larger lowercase letters
The difference is caused only by much wider letter spacing
options.misconception: blames tracking for a change in the height of letters

options.text: All faces render at an identical cap height at the same point size
options.misconception: assumes uniform vertical proportions across all typefaces

questions.explanation: X-height is the height of the lowercase body of a letter relative to the cap height. Two typefaces at the same point size can look different in size because one has a larger x-height, which makes its lowercase letters loom larger on the page.
